title: Tenant-aware telemetry routing and secure on-prem collectors for Dedicated & Private
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Dedicated and Private customers are asking for parity with hosted observability while preserving tenant isolation and meeting compliance for VPC/on-prem installs. Current collector prototype forwards OTLP traces and Prometheus metrics straight to hosted ingestion with a single credential and no per-customer scoping. That creates risks for cross-tenant leakage and insufficient controls for air-gapped installs.

Goal: Build a tenant-aware telemetry pipeline for Dedicated & Private that provides: (1) per-tenant isolation at the collector level, (2) secure transport (mTLS + signed tokens), (3) configurable sampling/pii-scrubbing policies, and (4) flexible routing: local retention for on-prem, conditional forwarding to hosted ingestion, or fanout to customer-preferred backends. Deliver accompanying dashboards for latency/error SLOs that operate in both hosted and private modes.

Success criteria / Acceptance:
- Collector enforces tenant scoping: traces/metrics/logs are tagged with immutable tenant_id and cannot be re-labeled upstream.
- mTLS + short-lived signed tokens enable mutual auth between services and hosted ingestion.
- Per-tenant rate limits and sampling policies are enforced at the collector and observable via metrics.
- Dashboards for per-tenant 95/99 latency, error rates, tail tokenization throughput exist and match queries in hosted environment.
- Air-gapped collector supports batched offload to USB/secure S3-compatible bucket for later ingestion.

Design summary:
- Collector: an extended OpenTelemetry-based binary that supports multi-tenant input endpoints, tenant lookup via X-Redwood-Tenant or mTLS SAN, and policy hooks. Collector acts as a reverse proxy for local retention (Prometheus remote_write + local file store) or OTLP/HTTP forwarder.
- Isolation model: immutable tenant metadata is injected at ingress. Collector will reject events without a valid tenant binding. Cross-tenant join features (global trace aggregation) will be opt-in via explicit operator config with audit logging.
- Security: mTLS between data plane components; token exchange using customer-managed KMS for Private installs (HSM/KMS integration task: ENG-8250). PII-scrub rules run on a policy engine with a minimal regex-based pipeline; sensitive fields are replaced with deterministic hashes.
- Sampling/routing: policy engine supports per-tenant head-sampling, tail-sampling for traces, and conditional fanout rules (example: forward errors and tail traces to hosted, keep metrics local).
- Observability: collector exposes Prometheus metrics (per-tenant ingestion rate, rejected-by-policy, cpu/memory, sampling-ratio) and tracing spans for collector processing. Dashboards will be materialized in the console and a fallback Grafana for on-prem.

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha: internal-only Dedicated pool (feature-flagged) to validate multi-tenant inject and mTLS handshake (week 1-2).
2) Canary: two willing customers on Dedicated, read-only retention for on-prem mode; monitor for rejections and perf impact (week 3-4).
3) GA: enable per-tenant routing controls in Console + docs + migration guide (week 5-8).

Migration notes: existing collectors will be rolled to the new binary with opt-in tenant enforcement. Provide a compatibility mode that accepts legacy token but adds a migration audit log.

Testing & Metrics:
- End-to-end tests that assert tenant isolation for traces and metrics (unit + e2e).
- Perf targets: <5% CPU overhead for typical 1000 rps ingestion and tail-latency for traces <50ms at collector processing.
- Monitoring: collector telemetry broken out by tenant; alert runbooks for high rejection-rate, metric backlog, and failed mTLS handshakes.

Docs & Links:
- Design spec: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aB-collector-tenant-aware-design
- GH PR (collector core): https://github.com/redwood-inference/collectors/pull/212
- Console dashboard draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/observability-dashboards

Open questions / Trade-offs considered:
- Where to perform PII scrubbing (edge vs hosted ingestion) — chosen to do minimal edge scrubbing to avoid sending raw PII upstream in Private installs.
- Sampling locality: prefer head sampling at collector for cost control, but keep tail-sampling hooks to capture error-related traces.
- Air-gapped export format: opted for encrypted tar of OTLP + manifest rather than proprietary binary for easier customer inspection.
